All frontend flows verified: admin login/dashboard tabs, chef creation & role-based redirect, chef dashboard, employee signup, holiday blocks booking, menu shown to employee, theme toggle, change password + re-login, forgot password success message, audit logs, email report endpoint. critical.issue: Always returns 400 'Reset link has expired' even with a fresh valid token. RCA: forgot_password stores tz-aware datetime (now_local()+1h in Asia/Kolkata) but Motor/MongoDB persists it as naive UTC datetime. In reset_password, code does `expires_at.replace(tzinfo=TZ)` on the naive value, effectively treating the UTC timestamp as Kolkata time. This makes the expiry appear ~5:30h in the past. Fix: in reset_password interpret naive stored datetime as UTC, i.e. `expires_at = expires_at.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` (then optionally .astimezone(TZ)).

action_items: Fix reset-password expiry timezone comparison in /app/backend/server.py (reset_password endpoint): naive datetimes read from Mongo must be interpreted as UTC, not TZ (Asia/Kolkata). E.g. `if expires_at.tzinfo is None: expires_at = expires_at.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)`. Once fixed, rerun test_reset_password_flow to verify.

rca of the issue: reset-password 400: `forgot_password` writes `expires_at = now_local() + 1h` (Asia/Kolkata tz-aware). Motor/PyMongo converts tz-aware dt to UTC then stores as naive BSON datetime. On read, `rec['expires_at']` has `tzinfo=None`. Code does `expires_at.replace(tzinfo=TZ)` — this labels a UTC clock reading as Kolkata (UTC+5:30), which is 5.5h earlier than the true instant. `now_local() > expires_at` therefore becomes true immediately, and the endpoint raises 400 'Reset link has expired'. Fix: replace with `timezone.utc` (or convert `now_local()` to UTC before comparing).
